metaDescription: Mabunga mungbean is a mungbean variety. About 62 days to harvest, 1.2 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Mabunga is a registered mungbean variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1996 as NSIC 1996 Mg 02. It takes about 62 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.23 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Mabunga mungbean takes about 62 days from sowing to harvest. That is about the average of the 33 mungbean varieties with a day count, 59.8 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.23 t/ha matches the average of its group, 1.25. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot).

The pests and diseases that hit mungbean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 6.5 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed.
Where and when to plant Mabunga mungbean

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Munggo is ready in about two months, so it fits the gap after rice. Pick a variety that ripens its pods together, which saves picking rounds, and one rated against cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 62 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.23 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Mabunga?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
